high_consensus.description: Real production gap. If stream=true is used, contract mismatch between /responses SSE events and chat chunks can break adapters immediately. Highly actionable via explicit event normalization spec and fixtures.
Important precedence ambiguity. Conflicting settings (explicit pin vs prefer_pro_models) will produce divergent implementations without a worked rule. Low effort to clarify, high consistency payoff.

Critical billing correctness issue. Reasoning-token accounting errors can materially distort cost controls, especially on pro tiers. Very high ROI to lock down with pre-implementation verification and anti-double-count tests.

Valuable test coverage request. Multi-turn tool_call/tool_result threading is a known complexity point for /responses typed inputs and can fail despite single-turn passing. Actionable and proportionate.

disputed.description: Important interaction test between two hard constraints (immutable alias pins vs pro preference). Prevents unintended cost/quality drift for legacy users. Focused and low implementation cost.

blockers.concern: Cost-risk controls are deferred to Sprint 3, but major alias flips happen in Sprint 2, creating a window where costs can drift without hard caps.
blockers.why_matters: Even with non-pro defaults, real usage patterns can spike spend post-migration; teams lack enforceable budget protection during MVP rollout.
blockers.location: Scope/Prioritization (Sprint 1+2 MVP) + FR-5 (cost cap in Sprint 3)
blockers.recommendation: Move minimum cost guardrails (session cap + alert threshold) into Sprint 2 launch criteria before default flips.

blockers.concern: Defaulting unknown/missing endpoint_family to chat creates silent misrouting risk for future models and can mask config errors until runtime failure.
blockers.why_matters: A typo or missing metadata can pass config load, then fail under production load with hard-to-diagnose 400s.
blockers.location: FR-1 Acceptance Criteria (unknown/missing endpoint_family defaults to chat)
blockers.recommendation: Make endpoint_family mandatory for OpenAI models (fail validation in CI), and only allow runtime defaulting for legacy entries explicitly marked as legacy.

blockers.concern: Response normalization scope is still incomplete: no explicit requirements for streaming responses, multimodal blocks, or future OpenAI response object variants.
blockers.why_matters: The adapter may work for current fixtures but break as soon as responses include new block types, leading to parsing failures or silent data loss.
blockers.recommendation: Add an extensible parser contract (unknown block passthrough + telemetry), include streaming and multimodal test fixtures, and define behavior for unsupported blocks.

blockers.concern: Rollback kill-switch is likely non-functional for gpt-5.5 models because forcing all OpenAI traffic to /v1/chat/completions will return HTTP 400 for those models.
blockers.why_matters: In an incident, the documented emergency control could worsen outage instead of restoring service, leaving no safe runtime fallback for gpt-5.5 traffic.
blockers.location: FR-1 Acceptance Criteria (operational kill-switch) + Risks/Mitigation table
blockers.recommendation: Redefine rollback as model-level failover (e.g., auto-retarget to gpt-5.3-codex or provider fallback), not endpoint coercion. Add an integration test that simulates incident mode and proves successful completion.

blockers.concern: The timeline is unrealistically compressed for multi-provider routing, schema changes, map regeneration, and backward-compat smoke across 3 sprints in 3 days.
blockers.why_matters: Schedule pressure increases risk of incomplete testing, rushed merges, and production regressions.
blockers.recommendation: Add buffer and explicit exit criteria per sprint, including soak period and canary rollout before default flips.
